comment: Cross-border exchange is described as relying on federated exchange through national gateways rather than a central supranational store. This is a useful pattern but should not be presented as the only legitimate architecture.

public.text: Cross-border exchange is described as relying on federated exchange through national gateways rather than a central supranational store. This is a useful pattern but should not be presented as the only legitimate architecture.
public.suggestedRevision: Present national-gateway federation as the preferred pattern in the cited examples while allowing other legally governed arrangements, such as regional services, shared repositories for limited datasets, or direct trusted-authority exchange.
